newsitem.title: UK: Lloyd's says reaches deal with Stephen Merrett.
newsitem.headline: Lloyd's says reaches deal with Stephen Merrett.

text.p: Lloyd's of London said on Thursday agreement had been reached with the insurance market's former deputy chairman Stephen Merrett, the underwriting agencies of the Merrett Group and the Merrett Syndicate 418 Names Association.
Lloyd's said in a statement that Merrett would personally pay 1.0 million stg to the Association and the agencies will pay Lloyd's approximately 2.2 million stg.
The Names' Association was set up by Names -- individual backers of the Lloyd's market -- who suffered huge losses through Merrett Syndicate 418.
The 2.2 million stg is the agencies' contribution to 225 million stg "contributed to the settlement by all underwriting agencies", Lloyd's added.
Last year Lloyd's secured agreement between Names and agencies in the market, ending several years of bitter conflict after the market sustained record losses.
Lloyd's said that after "extensive negotiations", Merrett, the underwriting agencies "become parties to the settlement under Lloyd's reconstruction and renewal programme".

Lloyd's said that Merrett would not, at any time, "be a director, employee or shareholder of any company in the Lloyd's market" and the Lloyd's inquiry into the conduct of Merrett and the Merrett agencies "will be terminated".
In addition Merrett will receive no debt credits in the settlement of his finality bill.

"Our agreement to this settlement has the overwhelming support of the committede of the Association who will be recommending acceptance by members at a meeting on 30 January," said John Mays, chairman of the Association.
Merrett was deputy chairman of Lloyd's in 1993 and part of 1994. During 1994 Lloyd's members' agents withdrew support for Merrett syndicates.
